about: Ulacia is a small family winery above the fishing port of Getaria, a few kilometers west of San Sebastián on the Basque coast. Founded in the 1940s and now run by the third generation, Julián and Amaia Ulacia, it farms about six hectares of cliffside plots directly above the Bay of Biscay and makes around 6,000 cases a year, much of it drunk locally in the bars and seafood grills of the region.

The wine is about 95 percent Hondarrabi Zuri with 5 percent of the red Hondarrabi Beltza, grown on clay over granite and trained high on the trellises typical of this very wet zone so that sea air can move through the vines. Grapes are hand-harvested and pressed as whole clusters, which keeps the red grape from tinting the wine. It ferments in steel tanks, rests about three months without lees stirring, and is bottled cold, straight from the tank, so it keeps the natural carbon dioxide from its own fermentation.

That light prickle is why txakoli is poured in Getaria from a height into a wide tumbler, raising a brief foam that lifts the aromas. The Ulacias’ white is made to be drunk young and cold and at the table, with the grilled fish, anchovies and shellfish that come in to the harbor below the vineyards.
facts: Hand-harvested, whole-cluster pressed, fermented in steel
